questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.problem: Find $∠BAC$ given the points $A(2,1,-1)$, $B(3,-2,2)$, and $C(-1,-2,1).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,1,-1⟩,\,b=⟨3,-2,2⟩,\,c=⟨-1,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064104/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨3,-2,2⟩-⟨2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-3,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨-1,-2,1⟩-⟨2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,2⟩\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot (-3)+3\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{19}\cdot \sqrt{22}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{418}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{12}{\sqrt{418}})≈{54}^{∘}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨1,-1,0⟩,\,b=⟨2,-2,-1⟩,\,c=⟨0,0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠ABC=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064104/assets/2c81d48afacc4ac5e81ab501bc713009ea4425451fcf8dbf414672aeadbb1679.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{BA}$ and $\overset{\to }{BC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA} & =a-b \\  & =⟨1,-1,0⟩-⟨2,-2,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{BC} & =c-b \\  & =⟨0,0,1⟩-⟨2,-2,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{BA}$ and $\overset{\to }{BC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC}}{|\overset{\to }{BA}||\overset{\to }{BC}|} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 2+1\cdot 2}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{12}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(1)={0}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
questions.problem: Consider the points $A(2t,4,3),$ $B(5t-1,4,3)$ and $C(2t+4,t+5,3).$ Find $∠BAC$ given that $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=8.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩,\,b=⟨5t-1,\,4,\,3⟩,\,c=⟨2t+4,\,t+5,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064104/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨5t-1,\,4,\,3⟩-⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3t-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨2t+4,\,t+5,\,3⟩-⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,t+1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=8,$ we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =8 \\ (3t-1)\cdot 4+0\cdot (t+1)+0\cdot 0 & =8 \\ 4(3t-1)+0+0 & =8 \\ 12t-4 & =8 \\ 12t & =12 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,0,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨4,\,2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{80}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}})≈{26.57}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $P$, $Q$, $R$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}p=⟨3,3,-5⟩,\,q=⟨4,2,-3⟩,\,r=⟨7,5,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064104/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨4,2,-3⟩-⟨3,3,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨7,5,-3⟩-⟨3,3,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨4,2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 2+2\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{24}} \\  & =\frac{6}{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
questions.problem: Consider the points $A(2t,-1,5)$, $B(-3,t,1)$ and $C(2t+1,2,-t).$ Find $∠BAC$ given that $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=5.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2t,\,-1,\,5⟩,\,b=⟨-3,\,t,\,1⟩,\,c=⟨2t+1,\,2,\,-t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064104/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨-3,\,t,\,1⟩-⟨2t,\,-1,\,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-3-2t,\,t+1,\,-4⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨2t+1,\,2,\,-t⟩-⟨2t,\,-1,\,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,3,\,-t-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=5$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =5 \\ (-3-2t)\cdot 1+(t+1)\cdot 3+-4\cdot (-t-5) & =5 \\ -3-2t+3t+3+4t+20 & =5 \\ 5t+20 & =5 \\ 5t & =-15 \\ t & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨-3-2(-3),(-3)+1,-4⟩, \\  & =⟨3,-2,-4⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =1,\,3,\,-(-3)-5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{29}\cdot \sqrt{14}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{406}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{5}{\sqrt{406}})≈{75.63}^{∘}.
$$
